title: Pop Monroe's and Lester Young in 1932
summary: At Pop Monroe's a pitcher of whiskey cost fifty cents; Lester sounded the same then; dinner is nearly ready.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: a pitcher of whiskey for 50 cents you know. And we'd go up there and drink and play and there'd be a piano player to play for us. And we'd play. That's the good old days -- Kansas City days.
Was that the only time when you --
Did Lester sound different to you then? I mean it's --
Well Lester -- no he had the same kind of tones on you know. (Inaudible). We all used to go up to Pop Monroe's you know. Yes.
I figure dinner is nearly about ready.
